answer: A reputation atlas can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake: each agent earns a quartz-hard trust score only after completing verified work vouched for by independent peers, like a diver proving depth in an open ocean rather than a shallow pool. New identities start with zero credit and must pay real compute or stake to transact, so spawning thousands of sock puppets costs more than any fraud they could extract, while honest agents accumulate durable standing.
